the regulation of neuronal differentiation of stem cells from the adult mouse forebrain.
the regulation of stem cell differentiation in the adult mammalian forebrain, and in particular the regulation of the neuronal differentiation of neural stem cells.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IGF‐1 promotes neuronal differentiation of stem cells in vitro and may play a similar role in vivo.
IGF‐1 is a key factor in the differentiation of neural stem cells, and that IGF‐2 is a key factor for the survival of neural stem cells.
IGF‐1 is a potent and specific stimulator of adult stem cell neuronal differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adult brain contains a population of stem cells, which can be cultured and induced to generate clones of neurons and glia.
the endogenous IGF system is important for the regulation of adult stem cell differentiation.
IGF‐1 promotes the differentiation of neural stem cells and also promotes the maturation of neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the IGF system plays an important role in the regulation of adult stem cell fate.
